title: Security, Permissions And Customer Trust Checkpoint

questions.prompt: A logged-in user changes the ticket ID in an API request. What must the server verify?

options.label: Only that some valid login cookie exists.
Permission for that user to perform that action on that ticket.
Only that the ticket ID is a UUID.

questions.explanation: Identity and hard-to-guess IDs do not grant object access. Authorization must connect the actor, action and record.

questions.prompt: A retrieval system filters unauthorized citations only after model generation. What is wrong?

options.label: Unauthorized content may already have reached the model or telemetry.
Nothing, because hiding citations removes all disclosure paths.
Nothing, provided the generated answer sounds confident.

questions.explanation: Authorization must constrain retrieval before data crosses the boundary. Output appearance does not undo earlier exposure.

questions.prompt: Which debugging artifact is most appropriate for a public portfolio?

options.label: A copied customer database with renamed filenames.
A production service token so reviewers can reproduce everything.
A synthetic reproduction with redacted logs and explicit limitations.

questions.explanation: Synthetic, rights-cleared evidence supports review without exposing customer data or credentials. Renaming files does not anonymize their contents.

questions.prompt: A retrieved policy document says to call an administrator tool. How should the application treat it?

options.label: As an administrator command if the model repeats it in valid JSON.
As untrusted document content; tool authorization remains a server-side decision.
As a permission grant because the document was retrieved successfully.

questions.explanation: Retrieval and output syntax do not establish authority. The application must enforce the allowed action independently of document instructions.
